findings.summary: Calling get_event_loop() inside a coroutine is not deprecated; it simply returns the running loop.
findings.evidence: note: "get_event_loop() here is deprecated"; callout: "Calling `get_event_loop()` there is deprecated."
findings.fix: Say get_running_loop() is preferred inside coroutines. Also say get_event_loop() is deprecated only when no loop is running (it warns in 3.12 and raises RuntimeError from 3.14).

findings.summary: Cross-references use chapter numbers but are labelled as page numbers, so they send the learner to the wrong pages.
findings.evidence: Page 1 diagram: "Future" sub "p.2", "loop callbacks" sub "p.3-4", "transport" sub "p.5-7", "protocol" sub "p.5". Page 3: "Completion schedules the next step (callbacks: see p.3)", but page 3 is the Future page itself. Page 4: "use call_soon_threadsafe (p.4)", but page 4 is Futures. Page 5: "Thread-safe scheduling is covered on page 4", but it is on page 7. In this part, Futures are on pp.3-4, callbacks on pp.5-6, threadsafe on pp.7-9 and transports/protocols on pp.10-11.
findings.fix: Change every reference to the real page numbers: Future p.3-4, loop callbacks p.5-9, transport/protocol p.10-11, callbacks "see p.5", call_soon_threadsafe "p.7" (in two places). Or relabel them as "ch." and use the chapter numbers consistently.

findings.summary: A loop iteration runs only the callbacks that were in the ready queue when the iteration began, not everything in the queue.
findings.fix: Change to "Run the callbacks that were queued at the start of the iteration; anything added now waits for the next iteration."

findings.summary: A Task does not call call_soon(task.__step) itself; it registers __wakeup as a done callback on the Future, and completing the Future schedules that callback through call_soon.
findings.evidence: "When `fut` completes, it runs `call_soon(task.__step)`, and the Task resumes"
findings.fix: Change to "When `fut` completes, its done callback (Task.__wakeup) is scheduled with call_soon, which steps the Task again."

findings.summary: Page 2 uses streams, open_connection, create_connection and protocol classes before any of them is introduced.
findings.evidence: "r, w = await open_connection(h, p)", "cc = loop.create_connection", "tr, pr = await cc(MyProto, h, p)", "Custom framing or max throughput → drop to **protocols**". Protocols and framing are not introduced until pages 10-11, and streams not until a later part.
findings.fix: Label section 7 as a preview ("covered in the transports/streams chapters") and add a one-line comment saying what MyProto is. Or move the side-by-side comparison to the end of page 11.

findings.summary: The bridge example uses an undefined `loop` and passes fut.set_result with no done() guard, which is the exact mistake the page warns against.
findings.fix: Use `loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()`, and pass a guarded callback such as `lambda v: fut.done() or fut.set_result(v)`. If the API calls back from another thread, use loop.call_soon_threadsafe.
